title: Personal Credit Cards: which autopay instruction stays on a card closed with a balance
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: autopay kept on a card closed while a balance remains

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line and reads the cardholder's checking account. When a cardholder confirms the closure of a card that still owes a balance, it decides whether the card's automatic payment instruction stays on the closed card.

## Entry condition for closing a card that still owes

A closing autopay instruction sits on an active checking account before a card that still owes a balance is closed. Its purpose is that the remaining balance is collected. Where a balance will remain and that condition is unmet, the closure is not confirmed.

## Rule

1. When a balance remains and the card's autopay source is a PCB checking account of the cardholder whose status is active, the card's autopay instruction as it stands at that moment is kept on the closed card.
2. When a balance remains but the card names no autopay source, or the named source is not active, the automatic payment left on the closed card is none.
3. A named source that cannot be found as a PCB checking account counts as not active.

The source account and its status are read from the bank's checking account records for the account named on the card.

## Branch table (a balance remains)

| Autopay source named on the card | Instruction left on the closed card |
|---|---|
| active PCB checking account of the cardholder | the card's instruction at that moment, unchanged |
| a checking account that is not active | none |
| no source named | none |
| a reference that matches no PCB checking account | none |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical cards)

- A card carrying a fixed amount instruction on an active checking account of the cardholder keeps that fixed amount instruction when it closes with a balance.
- A card carrying a minimum due instruction on a checking account that has since become inactive leaves none on the closed card.
